subject.title: fix(msteams): avoid memory spikes from oversized certificate files

question: What maximum PEM size should Microsoft Teams certificate authentication support before failing closed?
rationale: Azure Identity requires PEM certificate contents but defines no maximum, so choosing 64 KiB versus a larger bounded compatibility window determines whether existing operator certificate bundles continue to initialize. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/%40azure/identity/clientcertificatepemcertificate?view=azure-node-latest&utm_source=openai))

options.title: Approve 64 KiB
options.body: Keep the proposed ceiling as a generous bound for a certificate and private key, then implement it through the shared reader with boundary and partial-read coverage.

options.title: Use a larger bounded window
options.body: Select a larger explicit ceiling such as 256 KiB to accommodate unusually large certificate chains while still preventing material memory spikes.

recommendation.title: Approve 64 KiB
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed ceiling as a generous bound for a certificate and private key, then implement it through the shared reader with boundary and partial-read coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available recent Microsoft Teams runtime ownership signal for deciding the channel-specific compatibility boundary.
